buckets.name: Direct Air Capture
buckets.scope: Engineered systems capturing CO2 from ambient air, across all capture chemistries and form factors
variations: liquid solvent DAC (hydroxide capture + calciner regeneration)
liquid amino-acid / non-caustic solvent DAC
solid amine sorbent DAC (temperature-vacuum swing)
advanced/novel sorbent DAC (MOFs, zeolites, thin-film structured sorbents)
electrochemical pH-swing DAC (bipolar membrane electrodialysis, acid-base regeneration)
electro-swing adsorption DAC (redox-active quinone electrodes)
moisture-swing DAC and hybrid atmospheric-water-harvesting systems
calcium/lime-looping DAC (limestone carbonation-calcination)
passive and piggyback contactors (mineralizing surfaces, HVAC/cooling-tower air streams)
integrated DAC-to-fuel/material plants; early-stage membrane and cryogenic DAC

buckets.name: Biochar & Bio-oil
buckets.scope: Pyrolysis and hydrothermal conversion of biomass into stable carbon (char, bio-oil) for soils, storage, or materials
variations: industrial slow-pyrolysis biochar plants (continuous reactors, heat/power co-products)
gasification-route biochar with syngas/electricity co-generation
mobile and village-scale pyrolysis units for distributed agricultural residues
hydrothermal carbonization of wet wastes (hydrochar)
bio-oil deep-well injection for permanent storage
biochar soil-application networks and credit aggregators
biochar-embedded materials (concrete, asphalt, plastics, filtration media)
pyrolysis reactor OEMs and technology licensors

buckets.name: Biomass Storage & BECCS
buckets.scope: Harvested biomass stored on land or converted to energy with biogenic CO2 capture (burial, BECCS, waste-to-energy, fermentation)
variations: engineered terrestrial biomass burial (dry casks, vaults, trenches)
subsurface slurry injection of organic wastes
BECCS retrofits on biomass power and district-heat plants
purpose-built biomass carbon removal and storage (gasification to hydrogen/power + CO2 storage)
waste-to-energy CO2 capture (biogenic fraction)
ethanol and fermentation biogenic CO2 capture and storage
biogas/RNG upgrading CO2 capture for removal credits
pulp & paper and other biogenic industrial BECCS
carbon-storing engineered biomass building materials (fast-growing fiber panels, structural timber products)

buckets.name: Enhanced Weathering & Mineralization (land)
buckets.scope: Reacting CO2 with alkaline rocks and industrial wastes on land, via field spreading, tailings carbonation, and in-situ/ex-situ mineral storage
variations: cropland enhanced rock weathering (crushed basalt spreading)
alternative ERW feedstocks (olivine, wollastonite, brucite, returned-concrete fines)
mine tailings carbonation (ultramafic mining waste)
alkaline industrial residue carbonation for storage (steel slag, ashes, brines)
in-situ mineralization via dissolved CO2 injection into basalt
in-situ mineralization in peridotite/ultramafic formations
ex-situ accelerated carbonation reactors (acid-recycle loops, pressurized carbonation to storable or cementitious minerals)
microbial/biotic acceleration of soil mineral weathering

buckets.name: Ocean-Based CDR
buckets.scope: Marine pathways that shift seawater chemistry, strip CO2 from seawater, or sink biomass into the deep ocean
variations: electrochemical ocean alkalinity enhancement (acid extraction from seawater)
mineral ocean alkalinity enhancement (lime/olivine/carbonate dosing at outfalls and from vessels)
river and watershed liming
coastal enhanced weathering (olivine sand placement)
direct ocean capture (seawater CO2 stripping via electrodialysis/vacuum)
brine-based capture and mineralization (desalination brine alkalinity loops)
macroalgae/sargassum cultivation and deep-ocean sinking
terrestrial biomass sinking in anoxic basins
microalgae and ecosystem approaches (coastal pond cultivation with desert storage, iron fertilization, artificial upwelling/downwelling)

buckets.name: Point-Source Capture
buckets.scope: Capture equipment for fossil and industrial flue/process gases, from giant plants to small and mobile emitters
variations: amine solvent capture (incumbent licensors plus next-gen low-energy amines)
non-amine solvents (potassium carbonate, chilled ammonia, amino acids, ionic liquids, enzyme-catalyzed)
solid sorbent capture (MOF/zeolite filter beds, VPSA/TSA cycles)
membrane separation (polymeric and hybrid membrane-cryogenic)
cryogenic capture (CO2 desublimation/frost)
oxy-fuel combustion and Allam-Fetvedt supercritical CO2 power cycles
pre-combustion and inherent-capture routes (gasification, chemical looping, molten carbonate fuel cells)
calcium looping and indirect calcination for cement/lime kilns
modular small-emitter capture (containerized units, building exhaust, gensets)
mobile and maritime onboard capture (ships, trucks, locomotives)

buckets.name: CO2 Transport & Geologic Storage
buckets.scope: Moving CO2 and securing it underground: pipelines, ships, hubs, wells, and storage monitoring
variations: CO2 trunk pipelines and regional aggregation networks
CO2 shipping (liquefied CO2 carriers) with port liquefaction/buffer terminals
rail, barge, and truck CO2 logistics
onshore saline aquifer storage developers (Class VI projects)
offshore storage hubs (subsea saline formations and depleted fields)
depleted oil/gas field storage and CO2-EOR transition projects
storage site characterization, modeling, and monitoring tech (seismic, fiber-optic, downhole, satellite)
CO2 injection well services and specialty well engineering
novel storage media (CO2 hydrates, enhanced coal-bed storage, engineered caverns) — early stage

buckets.name: CO2 Utilization: Fuels, Chemicals & Bio-products
buckets.scope: Converting captured CO2 into energy carriers, chemicals, food, and solid carbon products
variations: thermocatalytic e-fuels (reverse water-gas shift + Fischer-Tropsch SAF and e-diesel)
CO2-to-methanol and methanol derivatives
power-to-methane (synthetic natural gas)
direct CO2/CO electrolysis to syngas and chemical intermediates
solar thermochemical fuel synthesis
gas fermentation and microbial CO2/CO conversion (ethanol, acetate, PHAs)
CO2-to-food (single-cell proteins, synthesized fats and ingredients)
CO2-derived polymers and polyols
CO2-to-solid-carbon products (carbon black, graphite, nanotubes, diamonds)
CO2-to-specialty chemicals (formic acid, oxalates, surfactants) and flue-gas-fed algae products

buckets.name: CO2 Utilization: Built Materials
buckets.scope: Locking CO2 permanently into concrete, aggregates, cements, and salable mineral products
variations: CO2 mineral curing/injection in ready-mix concrete and precast
carbonation of recycled concrete and demolition fines
synthetic aggregates from carbonated industrial residues (slags, ashes, air-pollution-control residues)
cement-free slag-based blocks cured with CO2
carbonated supplementary cementitious materials and recarbonated low-carbon cements
flue-gas direct mineralization to salable minerals (sodium bicarbonate, precipitated calcium carbonate, magnesium carbonates)
CO2-absorbing cement additives and coatings
